theorem.attribution: Binary instrumental-variable potential-response-type model; Wald ratio for complier LATE under instrument independence, exclusion and monotonicity; sharp ATE bounds from the finite response-type linear program.
theorem.scope: Binary instrument Z, binary treatment D, binary outcome Y, complete P(D,Y|Z) population law. Scientific assumptions require separate source-bound review.

verification_obligations: Negative and positive Wald effects within [-1,1]
Monotone latent-type compatibility before LATE point output
Separate reading and scientific reviews bound to the complete problem hash
ATE lower/upper primal feasibility, dual feasibility and strong duality
Independent verifier does not import the solver LP builder
Missing inputs, rejected/pending reviews, incompatibility and numerical failures remain distinct
limits: No non-binary instrument, treatment or outcome support
No automatic scientific assumption discovery or proof
Only reviewed binary IV candidate targets; unsupported structures/extra restrictions block execution; no automatic route fallback.

verification_evidence.note: Synthetic regression is not live business acceptance; see dated external execution evidence.

mapping.claim: Wald identifies the complier contrast under independent instrument, exclusion, monotonicity and positive complier mass.

mapping.locator: Section 2: finite response functions and linear programming; Section 3 bounds
mapping.claim: Finite response types encode the declared binary-IV model; optimizing the treatment contrast gives sharp model bounds.
